title: Adverbs of degree and manner — すこし／もっと／すぐ
summary: Adverbs go before a verb or adjective and show how much, how soon or in what way. Common N5 ones are すこし (a little), もっと (more), もう (already / more), すぐ (right away) and ゆっくり (slowly).

patterns.gloss: もっとゆっくり歩く (walk more slowly)
もうすこし (a little more), もうすぐ (very soon)

body.h: Degree: すこし and もっと
body.p: すこし means “a little”. もっと means “more”: もっとゆっくり (more slowly). もうすこし is “a little more”: もうすこし待ってください.

body.h: Time: すぐ and もうすぐ
body.p: すぐ means “right away”, and もうすぐ means “very soon (it will happen)”. もうすぐ電車が来ます (the train will come soon).
Adverbs sit right before the word they describe. They do not need a particle and do not change their form.

examples.ja: もう すこし 待（ま）ってください。
もっとゆっくり歩（ある）きましょう。
もうすぐ電車（でんしゃ）が来（き）ます。

pitfalls: もう has two meanings: “already” (with the past) and “more / again” (もう少し). Check the context.
Put the adverb before the word it describes, not after.
